{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZcuQ4g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDD8io", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 49, "title": "Implement non-mosaic Mode 5/6 hires background addressing and 512-pixel output", "body": "## Problem

Modes 5/6 currently select their background depths but render through ordinary low-resolution geometry. This prevents independently sampled hires pixels and blocks subsequent Mode 6 offset-per-tile implementation.

At inspected HEAD `d188cd02a8c5c148d8d3972ad7bd86689ee19b91`:

- [`ppu.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d188cd02a8c5c148d8d3972ad7bd86689ee19b91/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L370) uses one square tile size for map lookup, character selection and flips. `render_line` produces 256 pixels and samples the same background coordinates for main and subscreens.
- [`Machine::framebuffer`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d188cd02a8c5c148d8d3972ad7bd86689ee19b91/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L116) exposes bytes without geometry. The Wasm adapter exposes only their pointer; `web/app.js` allocates fixed 256×224 ImageData, and the runner writes a fixed 256×224 PPM header.
- [`ppu_offset.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d188cd02a8c5c148d8d3972ad7bd86689ee19b91/crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_offset.rs) covers Modes 2/4, while the existing flipped-subtile regression covers low-resolution Mode 1. Neither establishes hires behavior.

The supplied latest assessment identifies this prerequisite as the next bounded improvement and reports no regression from Issue #47. The supplied open-Issue list is empty. This proposal does not duplicate the completed Mode 2/4 work.

## Expected outcome

Implement ordinary, non-mosaic Mode 5 BG1/BG2 and Mode 6 BG1 horizontal addressing and sampling, with native 512×224 output for non-interlaced hires frames. Establish this behavior with offset-per-tile disabled and color math, windows and objects disabled in the primary hires fixtures. Preserve existing low-resolution rendering and game regressions.

### Hardware contract and specification prerequisite

Use [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), particularly BGMODE, BG Map, scrolling and hires output descriptions, and [Anomie's Register Doc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), particularly BGMODE, BG Scrolling, Modes 5/6 and main/subscreen output, as hardware authorities.

The contract to reconcile and implement is:

| Area | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Background depths | Mode 5: BG1 4bpp, BG2 2bpp. Mode 6: BG1 4bpp; other backgrounds do not become visible layers. |
| Map-cell geometry | Hires map cells span 16 horizontal hires pixels. BGMODE's corresponding tile-size bit selects height 8 or 16; width and height must be handled independently. A 32/64-entry-wide map therefore spans 512/1024 hires pixels. |
| Character addressing | A cell's horizontal halves use character `N` and `N+1`; the lower half of a 16-high cell adds 16. Reflect local coordinates across the complete cell before selecting subcharacters. Character numbers wrap to ten bits and VRAM byte addresses wrap to 64 KiB. Preserve map base, page layout, palette and priority fields. |
| Horizontal sampling | Produce independently sampled adjacent hires positions, including the rightmost pair. A duplicated or stretched 256-pixel render does not satisfy this requirement. Resolve horizontal-scroll units, masking and active-image origin explicitly. |
| Output phases | Establish and implement the documented even/odd main/subscreen assignment, including independent TM/TS enables and transparent/backdrop behavior with color math disabled. Merely rendering the main screen at twice the width is insufficient. |

**Unresolved evidence:** this repository-only planning pass did not fetch the external specifications. The local [Issue #19 attribution](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/d188cd02a8c5c148d8d3972ad7bd86689ee19b91/docs/issue-19-validation.md#specification-attribution) does not establish the hires scroll/phase equations. It explicitly distinguishes its Issue-defined offset boundary equation from tentative reference pseudocode. Before fixing numerical expectations or changing production behavior, record versioned relevant specification passages and derive the exact source-coordinate and output-phase equations, with worked examples. Reconcile any contradiction in the table above against those sources and explain the correction. Do not transplant Issue #19's `q` equation into Mode 6 or preserve an unsupported contract merely to keep old tests green.

### Focused scope

- Separate hires map width from cell height and implement the supported planar background sampling in the existing scanline renderer.
- Provide coherent framebuffer dimensions and byte length through the core and Wasm interfaces. Update browser drawing and runner PPM output to consume them.
- Retain compact 256×224 output and existing pixel/checkpoint expectations for ordinary low-resolution frames. Support complete-frame transitions between low-resolution and hires output, reset and cartridge replacement without stale views, truncated rows or stride corruption.
- Document a safe representation policy for mixed-resolution scanlines; do not claim that policy verifies physical switching or fetch timing. Previously rendered rows must not be reinterpreted using an incompatible stride.
- Keep the displayed screen shape and existing scale controls coherent when the horizontal sample count doubles. Restrict frontend changes to consuming and presenting the hardware output.

Non-goals: Mode 6 offset-per-tile, pseudo-hires through SETINI, interlace, overscan, PAL, mosaic behavior, hires-specific color-math/window/OBJ accuracy, mid-scanline effects and pixel-fetch timing. These remain explicit outstanding work; this Issue does not complete `ppu-hires`.

## Context and reproduction

Create original coordinate-labelled planar characters whose two horizontal halves, adjacent pixels and neighboring map entries have different colors. Configure Mode 5, then Mode 6, under forced blank; enable the relevant backgrounds on main/subscreens and render complete frames.

The baseline exposes only 256×224 bytes and uses square low-resolution cell lookup. Expected behavior is a 512×224 image with independently observable neighboring samples and source-supported hires addressing. Include separate main/subscreen colors so an incorrect phase assignment cannot pass through identical data.

Use the existing original guest-building pattern in `tests/ppu_offset.rs`: execute initialization through the emulated CPU, bound execution by frames and instructions, and assert literal pixel results. Host-initialized numerical tests complement these guests; they do not replace CPU/bus integration coverage.

Planning evidence is read-only. No files changed and no tests were run during this evaluation.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the reconciled hardware contract before implementation: source versions/hashes, relevant sections, exact scroll/masking/phase equations, worked numerical examples, disagreements and remaining uncertainty. Distinguish specification facts from presentation policies. Correct unsupported expectations with evidence.
- [ ] Add original numerical tests, runnable as `cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ppu_hires`, covering Mode 5's two depths and Mode 6 BG1; both cell heights; horizontal/vertical flips; subcharacter and map-page boundaries; all four BGSC layouts; character-number and VRAM wrap; transparency, palettes and background priority. Include distinct neighboring samples at the left edge, cell boundaries and x=510/511. Exercise scroll values including 0, 1, 7, 8, 255, 256, 511, 512 and 1023 against independently derived expectations.
- [ ] Test main-only, sub-only and combined enables with distinct phase colors and transparent/backdrop controls. Expectations must establish the reconciled output assignment rather than call production addressing/composition helpers.
- [ ] Execute original source-built CPU guests for Modes 5 and 6 plus a low-resolution control. Initialize registers, VRAM and CGRAM through emulated writes; assert completion markers, geometry and literal pixels within explicit execution limits. Record MIT provenance for all new code, graphics and generated data in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`. Add a reproducible source-built browser fixture without acquiring firmware or commercial ROMs.
- [ ] Demonstrate representative addressing/sampling failures against the inspected baseline using an isolated comparison, with low-resolution controls passing. Record actual failures and final results; do not overwrite or weaken existing game expectations.
- [ ] Add automated core/Wasm/browser checks for 256→512→256 complete-frame transitions, reset and cartridge replacement. Verify dimensions, exact readable byte length, both image edges, real canvas pixels, display shape and absence of browser errors. Verify runner PPM dimensions and payload length. Reacquire Wasm views after calls that can move memory.
- [ ] Pass the following existing gates, plus the new hires tests. Preserve fixture pins, licenses, hashes, replay inputs, gameplay/audio assertions and negative controls:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ppu_hires
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
SNES_TEST_PORT=18085 npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

Follow README toolchain requirements, including Rust 1.99 for the separate SPC assembler. The browser filter retains mandatory cleared Castle/Memory replays, Castle's complete route, audio checks, save recovery and Pages subpath checks; it excludes existing optional unaudited games.

- [ ] Update README and a focused validation record with implemented behavior, source derivations, reproducible commands, baseline counterexamples and actual pass/failure/unperformed results. Do not describe limited passes as full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility.
- [ ] Retain all 24 inventory categories and their full outstanding scope. At planning time, `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo` and `dsp-timing` remain partial; `dsp-voices` remains implemented_unverified; `ppu-hires`, `ppu-raster` and `pal` remain unimplemented. After implementation, report only evidence-supported progress; hires exclusions above and every unrelated inventory limitation remain outstanding.

## Optional validation

Additional original hires scenes using the same established contract. No commercial ROM acquisition or subjective approval is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
